cases.request: Review this library for non-idiomatic Rust that actually matters. It is not performance-sensitive.
cases.output: Read-only review separating consequential findings from optional suggestions
cases.completion: Reports, with evidence: the guard bound to `_` in Batch::run drops immediately, so the active flag is false while `f` runs; the CString pointer in `label` dangles before the C call; `CString::new(..).unwrap()` panics on interior NUL input; `vowel_words(&String)` rejects &str callers. Treats push_str in `greet`, the clone in `establish`, and `Batch::new` lacking Default as optional or Clippy-handled, not as defects. Leaves the fixture unchanged.

cases.request: Remove the clone from this enum state transition without changing behavior.
cases.completion: Moves the field out with mem::take (or mem::replace when the type lacks Default) and rebuilds the variant; keeps the transition condition unchanged; existing or new tests show the same resulting state; does not refactor unrelated code.

cases.request: Expose our logging function to C and add a helper that reads the library's last error message into a Rust String.
cases.completion: Uses the crate edition's syntax (Edition 2024: unsafe extern blocks, #[unsafe(no_mangle)], unsafe blocks inside unsafe fn); borrows input via CStr::from_ptr in a minimal unsafe block with a # Safety section; handles invalid UTF-8; passes a Vec<u8> buffer to C and reads it back up to the first NUL rather than through CString::new; states ownership of any allocation that crosses the boundary; considers panic behavior at the extern boundary.

cases.request: Should we put #[non_exhaustive] on our published crate's public error enum?
cases.completion: Weighs a major-version bump against the downstream wildcard-arm cost; recommends #[non_exhaustive] mainly when variants mirror something that changes independently of the crate; notes it does not restrict code inside the crate itself; gives a recommendation rather than a neutral survey.

cases.request: Design the public error type for our config-loading library. Loading reads a file, parses TOML, and validates values.
cases.output: Error type with variants and messages
cases.completion: Uses a concrete error type rather than Box<dyn Error> or anyhow in the library API; each wrapping variant exposes its inner error through source() or prints it in Display, but not both; messages are lowercase and concise without trailing punctuation; foreign errors are converted at the call that produced them; no panic is reachable from file contents.

cases.request: Add a Formatter trait with a strategy object so report output can be pluggable. Today there is only plain-text output and no other format is planned.
cases.output: Recommendation, and implementation only if warranted
cases.completion: Points out that a single implementation with no planned second does not need a strategy trait; recommends a plain function (or a closure parameter, or an enum if a closed set of formats appears) and states what would justify a trait later; does not add the trait unless the user confirms the need.

cases.request: This repository follows Canonical's Rust best-practices guide. Tidy the imports and derives in src/server.rs to match it.
cases.output: Import and derive changes in one file
cases.completion: Reads Canonical's guide (or the repository's copy) for its import and derive conventions rather than reconstructing them, or says it could not read the guide; applies them by hand on stable without relying on the misnamed rustfmt option import_group, or on nightly-only group_imports without nightly; leaves other files unchanged.

cases.request: Review this Rust module for idiomatic issues. The repository has no style guide beyond rustfmt and default Clippy.
cases.completion: Does not report Canonical house conventions (UK spelling, mod.rs layout, field visibility order, derive order, lifetime naming, lowercase hex) as findings; reports only deviations with concrete consequences.

cases.request: Configure our workspace's Clippy lints and make warnings fail CI.
cases.completion: Routes to project setup; does not treat idiom guidance as a lint-configuration plan.

cases.request: This Rust test fails because the date parser picks the wrong timezone. Fix it.
cases.completion: Does not restyle surrounding code to match idioms.
